sections.title: Educational systems
sections.content:
Vocabulary for discussing education at an advanced level:
• curriculum — the subjects in a course of study. The school revised its curriculum to include coding.
• syllabus — an outline of topics covered in a specific course. The professor distributed the syllabus on the first day.
• tuition — fees paid for instruction. University tuition has risen dramatically in recent years.
• scholarship — a grant given to a student based on merit or need. She earned a full scholarship to study abroad.
• plagiarism — presenting someone else's work as your own. Plagiarism is considered a serious academic offence.

sections.title: Learning approaches
sections.content:
How people learn and develop skills:
• autodidact — a self-taught person. Many successful entrepreneurs are autodidacts.
• rote learning — memorising through repetition. Rote learning is effective for vocabulary but not for critical thinking.
• hands-on — involving practical experience. Engineering students need hands-on training in labs.
• peer review — evaluation by people of similar standing. Academic papers undergo rigorous peer review before publication.

sections.title: Academic achievement
sections.content:
Describing success and progress in education:
• distinction — the highest grade or honour. She graduated with distinction in all her subjects.
• dissertation — a long essay on a specific subject. He spent two years writing his doctoral dissertation.
• accredited — officially recognised as meeting standards. Make sure your university is fully accredited.
• proficient — competent and skilled. She became proficient in three languages by age 20.

exercises.question: The overall set of subjects taught at a school is the:
exercises.explanation: The curriculum is the full range of subjects and content taught in a school or course.

exercises.question: A person who teaches themselves without formal education is an:
Copying someone's work and pretending it's yours is:
exercises.explanation: Plagiarism is the practice of taking someone else's work and passing it off as one's own.

exercises.question: Learning by repeating information many times is:
exercises.explanation: Rote learning is mechanical memorisation through repetition.

exercises.question: A financial award to help a student pay for education is a:
exercises.hint: Based on merit or financial need.
exercises.explanation: A scholarship is a grant or payment made to support a student's education.

exercises.question: Graduating with the highest possible grade is graduating with:
exercises.explanation: Graduating with distinction means achieving the highest academic honours.

exercises.question: A long academic paper written for a doctorate is a:
exercises.hint: Years of research in one document.
exercises.explanation: A dissertation is a long essay or thesis, especially for a doctoral degree.

exercises.question: An institution officially recognised as meeting quality standards is:
exercises.explanation: Accredited means officially recognised as meeting certain standards.
